analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is a decent engineering services exporter but the promoter holding of just 23.28% is an immediate dealbreaker for me — management has no real skin in the game. At ₹10,625 Cr market cap with 10% revenue CAGR and sub-13% ROE, there is no SMILE story here.
key_strengths: Revenue doubled from ₹4,132 Cr (FY21) to ₹7,360 Cr (FY25) driven by aerospace, defense, and rail verticals
Near-zero debt (D/E 0.07) with 5 consecutive years of positive OCF and FCF improving to ₹688 Cr in FY25
Diversified across geographies (North America, Europe, Asia Pacific) and end-markets, reducing concentration risk
key_risks: Promoter holding at 23.28% is a fatal SMILE flaw — founder alignment is absent, making long-term conviction impossible
Operating margin at 9.04% is thin for an engineering services firm; FY25 operating income fell to ₹1,138 Cr from FY24's ₹1,303 Cr despite revenue growth
Revenue CAGR of 10.1% over 9 years — a decade of effort for below-15% growth in a company targeting global engineering markets
red_flags: Promoter holding of 23.28% — I need minimum 50%; this company is promoter-less in spirit
Finance costs exploded from ₹16 Cr (FY16) to ₹93-116 Cr recently despite overall low debt — operational borrowings are creeping up
Other income collapsed from ₹147 Cr (FY18) to effectively zero in FY24 — the treasury cushion that used to boost reported profits is gone
analysis.detailed_analysis: Cyient operates in the right themes — aerospace, defense electronics, digitization — but executes as a services business that rents out engineering talent rather than owning intellectual property. That distinction matters enormously for multibagger returns: services companies face constant client budget scrutiny, currency headwinds, and attrition pressure. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.1% with ROE at 12.8% and margins at 9% tells me this is a plodding compounder at best, not a multibagger. The promoter holding at 23.28% is the single biggest red flag — when promoters don't own a majority of their company, their incentives diverge from minority shareholders. Large institutional ownership (DII 39.5%) means this stock already has professional investors pushing it around, eliminating the information edge I rely on. At P/E of 19x for 10% growth and low promoter backing, I simply see no reason to own Cyient.
